clue.text: A kitty making love in an apartment on a waterbed?

indicators.note: the word in says the token for love goes inside the flat

parts.note: an apartment is a flat
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A cat getting amorous in someone's flat, perched on a waterbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitty is a cash FLOAT, which the clue says is made from O (love) inside FLAT (apartment); A then goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying on a waterbed you are buoyed up by water, which is the playful question-marked example of floating.

clue.text: Shaking some projectiles

definitions.meaning: a case of arrows, read as a quantity of missiles

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is trembling; read as two words it is a single case holding arrows, a set of projectiles.

clue.text: Charged terrorist after watching bingo

indicators.note: read as two words, bin go, saying the letters of bin leave the name

parts.note: Osama bin Laden, the al-Qaeda leader

explanation.surface: A terrorist pays attention after a game of bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'bingo' splits into 'bin go': remove BIN from BIN LADEN. 'after watching' is padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded, and charged also means loaded, as a gun or a battery is.

clue.text: Design and build trade with firm following

indicators.note: following says the firm comes after the rearranged word
to build something is to construct or assemble it, so the word's letters are reassembled

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A design-and-build business, with a company running it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design and build' looks like a trade phrase, but 'build' is the anagram signal for TRADE, giving ARTDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a style of decorative design from the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Finally, hospital patient was under treatment for itchy feet

indicators.note: under treatment says these letters are worked on and reshaped
finally picks the closing letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: A hospital patient who has been under treatment finally gets restless.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters L and T of 'hospital patient' join WASUNDER; 'treatment' rearranges the lot. 'under' looks like part of 'under treatment' but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy feet is an idiom for a restless urge to travel, a longing to roam.

clue.text: Hairlines with centre parting recede and wear away

indicators.note: parting means splitting the word for recede so the letter sits between

parts.note: to abate is to subside or recede

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the nine-letter word

explanation.surface: Receding hairlines, with a centre parting, thinning away.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of HAIRLINES is L, its fifth letter; 'parting' puts it inside ABATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ablate is to remove material by erosion or melting, wearing it away.

clue.text: Going to put reader off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is going to make a reader lose interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to' reads as future tense, but 'Going' is the definition and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A going is a leaving, and a departure is the act of leaving.

clue.text: Phone with bum coin

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
a git is a contemptible person, British slang, as is a bum

explanation.surface: Making a call with a worthless coin.
explanation.walkthrough: GIT is British slang for an unpleasant or useless person.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringgit is the currency unit of Malaysia.

clue.text: Reaction to striker's own goal from such a defender

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the answer is fashioned by reworking the following words

explanation.surface: How a defender reacts when the opposing striker puts the ball in his own net.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SUCH A DEFENDER rearrange to the German word; 'from' signals the remaking, and the surface is nearly an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword means pleasure taken in someone else's misfortune, exactly what a rival feels at an opponent's own goal.

clue.text: US and England lay in ruins in days of yore

indicators.note: something in ruins is broken up, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: America and England left in ruins, as in olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' rearranges US, ENGLAND and LAY together into a Scots phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots phrase, known from the New Year song, means times long past, old long since.

clue.text: Second liaison featuring, at last, one cheap thrill

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

indicators.note: featuring means having something included, so the pair of letters goes inside

parts.note: a link is a connection or liaison

indicators.note: at last picks the final letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A second affair, one last cheap thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes E and P from 'one cheap', which 'featuring' puts inside LINK to make LEPINK.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tickled pink is to be delighted, so the verb phrase means to delight or thrill someone.

clue.text: A meeting place in the street

parts.note: a venue is a place where people meet or an event is held

explanation.surface: Somewhere to meet up out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street, often tree-lined, in a town.

clue.text: One virtually geocryptic

parts.note: the start of this made-up word shows the letters of ego rearranged, cryptically altered

explanation.surface: Someone almost a cryptic geographer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as instructions, the answer says change the word EGO; the result GEO opens the coined word 'geocryptic', whose 'cryptic' tips off the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self is virtually the same person, another version of oneself.

clue.text: Fahrenheit zero perhaps completed what the Earth did in the Ice Age

definitions.text: what the Earth did in the Ice Age

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: something completed is over, finished

explanation.surface: Zero degrees Fahrenheit, a temperature from when ice covered the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ZERO to give ROZE.
explanation.definitionFit: During the glacial period much of the planet's surface became covered in ice.

clue.text: Perspective relating to age and size? Get it fixed

indicators.note: fixed here means repaired or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about one's view of age and size, followed by a command to sort it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the definition to the fodder; 'fixed' rearranges SIZE GET IT.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword means the spirit of the times, the outlook characteristic of an era.

Nonconformist defeated Clegg in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: to beat Nick Clegg, the former Liberal Democrat leader and UK deputy prime minister

explanation.surface: A rebel overcomes a politician in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the UK's Liberal Democrats and was deputy prime minister 2010-15.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatniks were members of the 1950s Beat Generation, rejecting conventional society.

clue.text: Wealth is a barrier restricting disease

indicators.note: restricting means hemming something in, so the illness sits inside the barrier

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
flu, influenza, is a disease

explanation.surface: Riches act as a wall keeping illness at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is abundance of money and goods, prosperity.

clue.text: What might Lady Hillingdon do before considering her country's one wild shot?

definitions.text: What might Lady Hillingdon do before considering her country's

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lady Hillingdon, lying back and thinking of England, plus a wild shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Hillingdon is credited with 'lie back and think of England', on enduring sex dutifully; the definition stops at 'country's', and 'one wild shot' rearranges ONEWILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Her advice was to recline, then think of England, so reclining is what she does before thinking of her nation.

clue.text: Injured girl's arm

parts.note: cut means wounded, injured
a lass is a girl, with the apostrophe s as a link

explanation.surface: A girl's arm has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a body part but means a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, a weapon, as in firearm.

clue.text: Democracy cliches keep coming round

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so the answer is held across the two words

explanation.surface: Democracy's clichés keep recurring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cyclic recurs in cycles, coming round again and again.

clue.text: See 9
Substitute ending for the Four Seasons: a last waltz

indicators.note: ending for asks for the end letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A replacement finale for Vivaldi's Four Seasons: one final waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of THE, FOUR, SEASONS, A, LAST and WALTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means an inferior imitation used as a replacement.

clue.text: 50% off suit and shirts, of course

indicators.note: half price in a sale here means half of each word is cut, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: A half-price sale on suits and shirts, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of SUIT is SU and half of SHIRTS is SHI. 'of course' reads as 'naturally' but means served as a course.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese dish of vinegared rice is often served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: On debit, a little freedom?

indicators.note: freedom here frees the letters of the preceding words to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone in debt asks whether they deserve a bit of liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freedom' both signals the anagram of ONDEBITALITTLE and, with the rest, describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone allowed release on surety before trial has a little freedom, possibly on a debt of the bail sum.

clue.text: Hands back in exchange

indicators.note: back means returned, so the word for hands is read in reverse

parts.note: paws are hands, informally

explanation.surface: Handing back in exchange for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another.

clue.text: A bit of slapstick? It's cheap and vulgar

definitions.text: A bit of slapstick? It's cheap and vulgar

indicators.note: a bit of means a part of the text, so the answer is found within it

explanation.surface: Slapstick comedy dismissed as cheap and tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'slapstiCK? IT'S CHeap'; the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Art or objects regarded as tasteless and showy, often ironically enjoyed.

clue.text: One night in Paris with skinhead northerners

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
nuit is French for night
the head, or first letter, of skin

explanation.surface: A night in Paris spent with a skinhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a shaven-headed youth but is the head of 'skin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are peoples of the Arctic north of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.
